answer: An agent economy can require World ID Orb verification before any trade: a chrome iris scanner maps one living iris to one World ID, once per person worldwide. A forger minting a thousand fake agents needs a thousand real irises, not a thousand email addresses, and the orb's liveness check rejects printed irises and silicone copies while flagging the device. At about 5 per bought iris, a 1,000-agent farm costs 5,000 before earning a cent, so the cheap timber of bulk signup crumbles to umber dust while verified agents trade across an open meadow.
